findings.issue: humanize is implemented twice (server utils and app utils); the display-name rules ('mr-mime' → 'Mr Mime') must be kept in sync by hand across the two bundles.
findings.suggestion: Move it to Nuxt 4's shared/utils/ directory, which is auto-imported into both app and server code and exists for exactly this case.

findings.issue: Every page hand-declares an interface mirroring its server route's payload; if the route's shape drifts, TypeScript won't catch it and the failure surfaces at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Rely on Nuxt's inference for internal /api routes (useFetch/$fetch types come from the registered handlers), or export the types once from a shared/types file consumed by both sides.

findings.issue: The cache cap only evicts expired entries; if more than 5000 unexpired keys accumulate the map keeps growing (bounded today only by API cardinality).
findings.suggestion: Enforce the cap by evicting oldest entries regardless of TTL, or use an LRU.

findings.issue: Games list is built by spreading the gameNames Set twice and index-aligning it with a Promise.all result ([...gameNames][i]) — correct but brittle under refactoring.
findings.suggestion: Materialise const names = [...gameNames] once and .map over it for both the fetch and the mapping.

findings.issue: Refetches all 21 type records that allTypes() already fetched internally, relying on the 60s cache to make it free.
findings.suggestion: Have allTypes() return the records (or a records variant) so callers don't re-request what the helper already loaded.

findings.issue: Global :page-key="(route) => route.path" forces a full page remount on every path change with no explanation of why (it resets MoveTable sort state between Pokémon).
findings.suggestion: Add a comment stating the intent, or scope the reset to where it matters (e.g. :key on MoveTable keyed by pokemon id).

findings.issue: Plain anchor with @click.prevent + clearError instead of the documented NuxtLink/button + clearError({ redirect }) pattern.
findings.suggestion: Use <NuxtLink to="/" external @click="clearError"> or a button calling clearError({ redirect: '/' }) for consistency with Nuxt's error-page docs.

findings.issue: setFilter reads route.query for unchanged filter keys at call time; a type-ahead keystroke racing an uncommitted router.replace can persist a stale q or drop the last character.
findings.suggestion: Build the query from the component's own filter refs (search/typeModel/generationModel) rather than from route.query.

findings.issue: All 441 lines of component styling live in one global stylesheet, so rules like .card/.panel/.badge are maintained far from PokemonCard/PageSection/TypeBadge.
findings.suggestion: At minimum split per-component blocks into scoped <style> in the SFCs, which is what Nuxt favours; tokens.css can stay global.

findings.issue: A ?game= value the Pokémon doesn't have silently falls back to the default game while the bogus value stays in the URL, so URL and UI disagree.
findings.suggestion: Either replace the query with the resolved default or ignore the unknown value consistently in the select's rendering.

summary: A clean, current Nuxt 4 app that uses the framework's real structure and primitives (app/ srcDir, server routes + useFetch, useHead/useId, URL-driven filter state, createError 404s) with careful correctness work around caching, sorting and 404 handling. The merge-blocking-ish items are maintenance smells rather than bugs: humanize duplicated across the server/app boundary where shared/utils exists, and page interfaces hand-mirroring server payload shapes instead of shared/inferred types. I'd approve after a nits round.
